title: ‘Our new normal’: how marine heatwaves affect life in British seas

paragraphs.en: ‘It sounds silly but I thought it was a person in the water waving,” says Kurt Lander, skipper of the Yellowfin charter boat, based out of Brighton. But when he grabbed his binoculars, he realised the fluttering movement he had noticed in the middle of the Channel shipping lane was a pair of sunfish.
paragraphs.zh: “听起来很傻，但我以为那是水里有个人在挥手。”以布赖顿为基地的黄鳍号包船船长库尔特·兰德说。但当他抓起望远镜时，他才意识到，自己在英吉利海峡航道上注意到的那阵摆动，其实是一对翻车鱼。

paragraphs.en: The huge fish were lying on their sides and flapping their fins. “Apparently, they do it as a visual attraction to birds,” he says. “They’re trying to get the birds to eat the parasites off them.”
paragraphs.zh: 这些巨大的鱼侧着身子躺着，拍打着鱼鳍。“显然，它们这样做是为了在视觉上吸引鸟类。”他说，“它们是想让鸟来吃掉它们身上的寄生虫。”

paragraphs.en: Lander has seen the huge fish with their unusual round bodies before. But the difference is that those that he spotted this year are part of a surge in sightings of the species off British shores this summer, probably as a result of a marine heatwave.
paragraphs.zh: 兰德以前也见过这种身形圆润独特的巨型鱼类。但不同的是，他今年看到的这些，只是这个夏天英国海岸附近这一物种目击数量激增的一部分，这很可能是一轮海洋热浪造成的结果。

paragraphs.en: The extraordinary temperatures are causing shifts in marine life far beyond an increase in sunfish. Some species are moving away from warmer waters, other “invaders” are appearing for the first time around Britain’s coastline, while some marine life is dying off under the rays of the sun.
paragraphs.zh: 异常的高温正在引起海洋生物的变化，远不止是翻车鱼增多而已。一些物种正在离开较暖的水域，另一些“外来入侵者”首次出现在英国海岸附近，而还有一些海洋生物正在阳光照射下死去。

paragraphs.en: Lander notices the change in the species of fish he now lands. “I used to catch at least a couple of hundred cod a year,” he says. Now, bringing in cod is rare. If he catches any, he adds, “it’s probably about one or two a year in the summer.”
paragraphs.zh: 兰德注意到他现在捕捞上来的鱼种发生了变化。“我以前每年至少能捕到几百条鳕鱼。”他说。如今，捕到鳕鱼已十分罕见。他补充说，如果还能捕到，“现在夏天大概一年也就一两条。”

paragraphs.en: Colder water species are just nowhere to be seen off the southern coastline, says Dr Zoe Jacobs, a senior researcher at the National Oceanography Centre in Southampton. Shifting their range to cooler seas farther north, they are now thriving in Scotland. “Temporarily or permanently, we don’t know,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: 南安普顿国家海洋学中心的高级研究员佐伊·雅各布斯博士说，喜欢冷水环境的物种如今在南海岸已经完全见不到了。它们将活动范围转移到更北的较冷海域，如今在苏格兰繁衍生息。“是暂时还是永久性的，我们不得而知。”她说。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Lander is catching more warm-water fish, such as bass, comber and triggerfish. According to last year’s State of the South-West Seas report , other species found in warmer waters – such as sardines and anchovies – are also doing well.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，兰德捕获的温水鱼类越来越多，比如鲈鱼、双带鱚（comber）和扳机鱼。根据去年的《西南海域状况报告》，其他出现在较暖水域的物种——比如沙丁鱼和鳀鱼——也长势良好。

paragraphs.en: Gio Reale , a diver based in the Cornish port of Falmouth, says: “Small water temperature changes have such big effects on marine life.” It has been weeks since he last saw his favourite shark species: the small spotted catshark (also called the lesser-spotted dogfish). These small sharks – which grow no bigger than a metre and are spattered with delicate freckles – prefer water temperatures of about 16-17C (61-63F).
paragraphs.zh: 常驻康沃尔郡法尔茅斯港的潜水员焦·雷亚莱说：“水温的微小变化就能对海洋生物产生如此巨大的影响。”他已经好几个星期没见过自己最喜欢的鲨鱼种类：小型斑纹猫鲨（也称小斑狗鲨）了。这些小型鲨鱼——最大不会超过一米，身上布满了精致的斑点——偏爱约16至17摄氏度（61至63华氏度）的水温。
